title: Answer a payout run again without paying it twice

blocks.text: This picks up where the previous practice ended, and the file already contains its solution.

Last night the node was restarted in the middle of the payout runs, and the operator moved everything in `payouts/run/` back to `payouts/request/`. This morning two merchants called to say they were paid twice. The same week, the acquirer resent a run by hand under a new file name, and it was paid again too.

The `Ledger` is a database: it survives restarts, and each `pay` records the run together with its payments. In `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PayoutProcessor.java`, finish `runOf` and `alreadyPaid` so that a run reaching the processor again is answered as before and pays nobody, whatever its file is called. A run number that comes back with different payouts is a problem for a person, not a repeat. About six lines in total.
The tests restart the node by building a new `DirPoll` and processor on the same directories and the same ledger.

cases.says: two different runs are both paid and answered
a run processed again after a restart is answered with its totals and pays nobody a second time
a run is identified by its content, so the same run under another file name is not paid again
the run's identity includes who sent it, so another acquirer's run with the same number is paid
a known run number carrying different payouts is not a repeat: it goes to a person and nobody is told it was paid

origin.section: 17.4 A Stop or a Crash Leaves Files in `run/`, Some of Them Already Done

concepts: Processing must be idempotent, keyed by the batch's identity in its content and recorded with the postings, never by the file name.
